scenes.query: night sky stars slow moving clouds
scenes.vo: What if you could solve a hard problem in your sleep, on purpose?
scenes.title:
Can you solve
a problem
in your sleep?

scenes.query: sleep laboratory brain scan electrodes person sleeping
scenes.vo: This year a team at Northwestern decided to actually test it. They handed twenty experienced dreamers a stack of tricky brain teasers, and quietly paired each puzzle with its own little soundtrack.
scenes.title:
So a lab
ran the test

scenes.query: abstract blue brain waves glowing dark
scenes.vo: Then, deep in REM sleep, the researchers softly replayed one of those sounds. And three out of four dreamers began dreaming about the exact puzzle it was tied to.
scenes.title:
The dream
took the bait
scenes.sub: dreamed about the very puzzle they were cued with

scenes.query: morning light waking up window calm
scenes.vo: And here is the part that really matters. The puzzles they had dreamed about were solved forty two percent of the time the next morning. The ones left out of the dream, only seventeen.
scenes.title:
And they solved
more of them

scenes.vo: One moment stayed with the scientists. A sleeping volunteer, not even aware they were dreaming, turned to a figure inside their own dream and simply asked them for help.
scenes.title:
One dreamer asked
for help
scenes.sub: inside the dream, a character was handed the puzzle

scenes.query: person lying awake in bed at night thinking
scenes.vo: So here is the thing to sit with tonight. Your mind does not clock out the moment you do. If it keeps quietly turning over whatever you fed it last, what problem would you choose to carry into the dark?
scenes.title:
What would you
hand to the night?
scenes.sub: the mind keeps working long after you close your eyes

scenes.query: milky way galaxy stars night sky
scenes.vo: Maybe sleeping on it was never really just an expression.
scenes.title:
Sleep on it,
literally
scenes.sub: ☾  the science of the everyday mind
